content_html:
Does Consciousness Create Reality?

There is a spectrum: from constructivist (reality-for-us is built) → idealist (reality itself is consciousness). Quantum and Buddhist views occupy the middle ground: emphasizing co‑arising or entanglement between mind and world. Scientific realism pushes back: consciousness models but does not make reality.

Perspective Core Claim How Consciousness Relates to Reality Representative Figures / Traditions Critiques
Constructivism Science / Phenomenology Perception and experience are actively built, not passively received. Reality-as-experienced is a construction of consciousness (predictive processing, memory reconsolidation). Husserl; Merleau-Ponty; Karl Friston; Andy Clark. Does not imply external world is absent—only that our access is constructed.
Idealism Philosophy Consciousness is the foundation of existence. Reality itself is mind-dependent; matter is derivative. Berkeley; Kant (transcendental idealism); Hegel; Kastrup (analytic idealism). Difficult to reconcile with scientific realism; risks solipsism.
Quantum-linked views Physics Observation is entangled with reality at the quantum level. Consciousness (or measurement) selects from possible states. Wheeler (participatory universe); QBism; Wigner’s mind-body proposal. Contested: many physicists argue “observer” need not mean consciousness.
Buddhist & Non‑Western Religion / Philosophy Phenomena arise dependently; reality is inseparable from consciousness. Madhyamaka: emptiness = no inherent essence; Yogācāra: mind-only; Vedānta: ultimate reality is consciousness (Brahman). Nāgārjuna; Vasubandhu; Śaṅkara. Critics: may collapse subject/object distinction too far for empirical inquiry.
Scientific realism Counterpoint There is an external world independent of consciousness. Consciousness constructs our model of reality but does not generate it. Most contemporary neuroscience & physics; Daniel Dennett; Patricia Churchland. Explains illusions as limits of construction, but assumes matter exists regardless.

A conceptual spectrum from scientific realism/constructivism (mind models reality) through co‑arising/interdependence, to idealism (reality is mind):
